changes.description: Renamed from `hex_aggregate` to `aggregate_points_to_h3_cell`. The old identifier keeps resolving: a saved workflow naming `hex_aggregate` is rewritten on open and stamped with sourceMigration, because the operation is unchanged and a rename must not refuse work the way a retirement does. The verb came after its object and the areal unit was unstated, while its sibling said verb first. Both now read as one operation over a named unit: aggregate points to H3 cells. The unit is the ontology's own term (fw:HexCell, 'H3 cell'), not 'hexbin', because a plotting library's hexbin is a lattice fitted to its data and these cells come from a fixed global index. No contract change: ports, output, parameters and behaviour are identical.

Retitled from "Group points in H3 cells". The node type names hexagonal aggregation and the title named the indexing method instead, so the two shared no word and a reader had to know that H3 cells are hexagons to connect them. Flagged by the naming ratchet added 2026-10-13 under title-type-agreement; the convention's own rule is that the node type and the title must say the same thing. No contract change: ports, output, parameters and behaviour are identical, which is why this is a patch.

evidence.note: Structural and deterministic checks only. No privacy guarantee or independent scientific certification.
